summary: The root طمأن (TmAn) primarily means to be or become quiet, tranquil, or at rest, especially after movement or disturbance.
lane: مأن مانهم مَأَنَهُمْ 1 He sustained them; bore the burden of, or undertook, their maintenance; he maintained them. (S, K, arts. مأن and مون.) === مَأَنَ القَوْمَ and ↓مَأَّنَهُمْ He maintained, or sustained, the people, or party. (M.) مأ مَأََّ 2 see 1. مانة مَأْنَةٌ of the belly: see جَأْبَةٌ. === المَأْنَتَانِ of the hump of a camel: see قَحَدَةٌ. مؤنة مُؤْنَةٌ i. q. قُوْتٌ [Food, &c.]; (M;) a dial. var. of ↓مَؤُونَةٌ (q. v.); as also مُونَةٌ: pl. مُؤَنٌ. (Msb.) مئنة مَئِنَّةٌ : see art. ان, where will be found the explanations of this word given in the S and K in art. مأن. مؤونة مَؤونَةٌ A weight, or burden. (Mgh, Msb.) See مِثْقَالٌ. === Trouble, molestation, or embarrassment; as also ↓مُؤْنَةٌ: pl. of the former مَؤُونَاتٌ; and of the latter مُؤَنٌ. (MA.) === The requisite means of subsistence. (KL.) === مَؤُونَةُ الجِمَاعِ: see زَافِنَةٌ: it seems to mean the pudendum muliebre considered as the means of جِمَاع.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here. Kitab al-Ayn does the same, and also files some weak roots under a different third radical; those are resolved against the Corpus spelling and the al-Ayn headword is kept in the entry.
